rules.statement: An appeal is rejected when the appellant fails to give notice of tendering security for the respondent's costs in a prescribed form, and this failure cannot be excused even if no objection was raised at the trial court.
rules.supporting_quote: "Where a statute prescribes that notice should be given to a party to a suit and indicates the form in which that notice should be given, that :notice should comply with the requirements of the statute and should be in the prescribed form. A schedule in a statute is as much a part of the statute and as much an enactment as any other part2[Reg. v. Lumsdaine, (1839) 10 A. & E. 157 at 160 ; 8 L. J. M. C. 69 at 71. Attorney General v. Lamplough, (1878) 3 Ex. D. 214 at 229 ; 47 L. J. Ex. 555 at 562]."
